explanation.text: The Logic: An "at-the-money" (ATM) option is one whose strike price equals the current spot price of the underlying. Saying ATM has zero delta or infinite gamma misstates standard option behaviour (an ATM call's delta is approximately 0.5; gamma is finite and peaks near ATM). Note: Option moneyness and Greeks are not defined in the PMS Distributors (XXI-A) derivatives chapter, which is limited to derivative definitions, purposes, settlement, margins, and PMS-derivative permissions. Treat this as general option theory; deeper options/Greeks coverage is in NISM Series VIII.
